title: Gas Price Collusion: Cross-Country Markups, Rockets & Feathers, and Repeated Oligopoly Supergames
model: Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon · High Thinking + Google Search + Pandas)

countries.regime: Algorithmic tacit collusion (+28% duopoly margin, Assad et al. 2024 JPE)
Rocket-and-feather margin expansion (+6 p/L CMA 2023–2025 finding)
BP focal-point signaling ended Edgeworth wars (+75% margin, Byrne & de Roos 2019 AER)
Mandatory price-disclosure portal increased local margins (+7%–11%, Luco 2019 AEJ)
High tax wedge + concentrated highway auction leases
Highest OECD pump price (62% sovereign tax + 24 c/L synchronized list price)
Parallel recommended price lists with regional sticky spreads
Loss-leader hypermarkets compress urban margins; highway corridors stay oligopolistic

countries.dominantFirms: ENEOS (~50%), Idemitsu Showa Shell, Cosmo Oil
Costco, QuikTrip, Wawa, Sheetz, Buc-ee's, 60%+ independents
countries.regime: Competitive high-volume discounters break focal-point coordination (12 c/L spread)
Administratively capped domestic fuel price below export parity

industries.whyMechanism: AI repricing detects rival cuts in seconds (T -> 0), eliminating deviation windfall and expanding duopoly margins +28% (Assad et al. 2024).
Inelastic aggregate demand (-0.15) maximizes joint collusive profit, while hyper-elastic station switching (-36% per 2 c/L) makes punishment devastating.
High weight-to-value creates tight 50 km geographic oligopolies with high multi-market contact and symmetric kiln capacities.
Spectrum auction barriers lock N=3; public rate cards allow instant matching of promotional discounts across flanker brands.
Multi-market contact across thousands of SKUs and shared wholesale suppliers sustains focal-point retail price floors.
Instant fare visibility aids coordination, but perishable empty seats at departure create strong temptations to dump last-minute fares.
Maverick big-box clubs optimize store membership/foot-traffic rather than fuel margin, refusing to join focal-point price jumps (delta < delta*).
Secret off-list discounting (Stigler 1964) means rivals cannot tell if a lost deal was due to price undercutting or product fit (large T, low delta).

industries.industry: Custom B2B Precision Manufacturing & Job Shops
industries.whyMechanism: Every RFQ has custom engineering specs and sealed bids; no common focal price exists and cheating cannot be monitored.
Even with N=2, orders are huge, lumpy, and infrequent ($10B fleet deals): a single deviation locks in 20 years of fleet aftermarket revenue.

pandasScript:
"""Reproducible Pandas analysis for ST-06: Gas Price Collusion & Oligopoly Supergames."""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# 1. Load the cross-country pump price decomposition & concentration table
countries = pd.read_csv("studies-gas-countries.csv")
countries["ex_tax_price_usd_l"] = countries["wholesaleUsdL"] + countries["markupUsdL"]
countries["tax_share_pct"] = (countries["taxUsdL"] / countries["pumpUsdL"] * 100).round(1)
countries["lerner_ex_tax_pct"] = (countries["markupUsdL"] / countries["ex_tax_price_usd_l"] * 100).round(1)
countries["excess_markup_vs_us_cpl"] = ((countries["markupUsdL"] - 0.12) * 100).round(1)

# Exclude state-capped producer monopoly (DZ) when estimating market oligopoly HHI gradient
market_oecd = countries[countries["code"] != "DZ"].copy()
corr_cr4 = market_oecd["cr4Pct"].corr(market_oecd["markupUsdL"])
corr_hhi = market_oecd["hhi"].corr(market_oecd["markupUsdL"])
slope_cpl_per_10pct_cr4 = np.polyfit(market_oecd["cr4Pct"], market_oecd["markupUsdL"] * 100, 1)[0] * 10

print("=== Cross-Country Oligopoly Markup Summary (Pandas) ===")
print(market_oecd[["code", "pumpUsdL", "wholesaleUsdL", "taxUsdL", "markupUsdL", "cr4Pct", "hhi", "lerner_ex_tax_pct"]])
print(f"Correlation(CR4, Ex-Tax Markup): r = {corr_cr4:.3f} | Correlation(HHI, Markup): r = {corr_hhi:.3f}")
print(f"OLS Gradient: +{slope_cpl_per_10pct_cr4:.2f} cents/L markup per +10 percentage points in CR4 concentration\n")

# 2. Asymmetric Pass-Through ("Rockets & Feathers" Error Correction Model)
pt = pd.read_csv("studies-gas-pass-through.csv")
rocket_half_life = pt.loc[pt["rocketPassPct"] >= 50, "day"].min()
feather_half_life = pt.loc[pt["featherPassPct"] >= 50, "day"].min()
cumulative_wedge_cpl_days = np.trapezoid(pt["rocketPassPct"] - pt["featherPassPct"], pt["day"]) / 10.0
print(f"Rocket 50% pass-through lag: {rocket_half_life} day(s) vs. Feather 50% decay lag: {feather_half_life} days")
print(f"Asymmetric tacit rent per 10 c/L wholesale cycle: +{cumulative_wedge_cpl_days:.1f} cent-days/L\n")

# 3. Repeated Bertrand Supergame Incentive-Compatibility (delta >= delta* = 1 - 1/N)
ind = pd.read_csv("studies-gas-industries.csv")
ind["collusive_spne"] = ind["deltaEff"] >= ind["deltaStar"]
print("=== Supergame Incentive-Compatibility (delta_eff vs. delta_star) ===")
print(ind[["id", "industry", "firmsN", "deltaStar", "deltaEff", "slack", "collusive_spne"]])
